skill.name: venue-templates
skill.description: Prepare venue-specific academic submissions using bundled LaTeX templates, formatting references, and helper scripts for journals, conferences, posters, and grant proposals.
skill.summary: Generate and check academic manuscript, poster, and grant templates for common submission venues.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by LaTeX math, Markdown code fences, documentation links, and benign helper-script patterns. No prompt injection or malware intent was found, but the skill encourages default use of an external AI diagram workflow that may expose unpublished research details.

remediation.issue: External AI schematic generation is suggested by default.
remediation.suggestion: Make schematic generation opt-in and require explicit user consent before sending research details to another skill or external model.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts can overwrite user-chosen output paths.
remediation.suggestion: Add overwrite prompts or refuse existing output paths unless a clear force option is supplied.

remediation.issue: PDF validation invokes local Poppler tools on user-supplied files.
remediation.suggestion: Document that untrusted PDFs should be validated in a sandbox and add subprocess timeouts.

semantic_findings.title: Implicit External AI Diagram Generation
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md recommends using another schematic-generation skill by default for new documents. For unpublished manuscripts or grants, this can disclose research details to an external AI workflow without explicit consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly direct users to another AI-powered schematic workflow and say new documents should generate schematics by default. The risk is privacy exposure rather than code execution, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: Academic submissions often fail because venue rules are hard to compare and easy to miss. This skill provides LaTeX templates, formatting references, and helper scripts for papers, posters, and grant proposals.
actual_capabilities: Provides bundled LaTeX templates for Nature, NeurIPS, PLOS ONE, research posters, NSF proposals, and NIH Specific Aims.
Summarizes formatting requirements for journals, conferences, posters, and major grant agencies.
Searches available templates by venue, type, or keyword with query_template.py.
Customizes template placeholders for title, authors, affiliations, and email.
Checks compiled PDFs for page count and font metadata when pdfinfo and pdffonts are installed.
Links to official author and grant guideline pages for manual verification.
limitations: Venue requirements can change, so users must verify final rules on official pages.
Only the bundled LaTeX files are directly available; many referenced venues are guidance only.
PDF margin validation is informational and requires manual review.
Helper scripts require local Python and optional Poppler tools.

use_cases.title: Submit A Journal Manuscript
use_cases.description: Select a journal template, review key formatting rules, and prepare a manuscript checklist before submission.

use_cases.title: Prepare A Conference Paper
use_cases.description: Compare conference page limits, anonymization needs, citation style, and template files before drafting.

use_cases.title: Draft A Grant Proposal
use_cases.description: Use NSF and NIH templates to organize required sections and formatting constraints for a proposal.

prompt_templates.title: Find A Template
prompt_templates.prompt: I am submitting to [venue]. Show the available template, key formatting rules, and files I should use.

prompt_templates.title: Customize A Manuscript
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the [venue] template and prepare a customization plan for my title, authors, affiliations, abstract, and section placeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Validate A PDF
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my compiled PDF for [venue]. Report page count, font notes, margin requirements, and manual checks I still need.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Submission Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [venue A], [venue B], and [venue C] for page limits, citation style, anonymization, figures, and template fit.

output_examples.input: I need to prepare a Nature manuscript.
output: Check abstract length, figure quality, citation style, and final author guidelines.
Verify current requirements on the official Nature author page before submission.

output_examples.input: What should I check before submitting to NeurIPS?
output: Confirm the page limit, anonymization status, two-column format, and reference policy.
Use the NeurIPS template notes and validate the compiled PDF before upload.
Review current conference instructions because annual rules may change.

output_examples.input: Help me start an NSF proposal.
output: Use the NSF proposal template and organize the project summary, project description, and broader impacts sections.
Check page limits, font requirements, margins, and required supplementary documents.
Confirm the current PAPPG rules before final submission.

best_practices: Verify current official guidelines before final submission.
Compile a clean copy of the template before adding research content.
Keep venue formatting separate from content revisions until final checks.
anti_patterns: Do not assume all venues in the reference notes have bundled templates.
Do not change margins, font size, or spacing to force content into a limit.
Do not send unpublished details to external diagram tools without consent.

faq.question: Does this include official templates for every listed venue?
faq.answer: No. It bundles selected templates and provides reference notes for many more venues.

faq.question: Can it update rules automatically?
faq.answer: No. It includes static guidance and links. Users must verify current requirements.

faq.question: Can it compile LaTeX documents?
faq.answer: It provides command guidance and validation scripts. Compilation depends on local LaTeX tools.

faq.question: Does it support grants?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes NSF proposal and NIH Specific Aims templates plus grant requirement references.

faq.question: Can it check margins accurately?
faq.answer: Only partially. The validation script reports required margins and recommends manual verification.

faq.question: Is it useful in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes instructions and files that these supported tools can read and apply.
